title: Review of c22's crawler front re-nucleation on fresh seeds 24-27: after a 40% front cut every cell passes through a non-polar disk (t~9.0-9.8) and re-nucleates a front, crawling on at 0.35 (0.42 before the cut) on a new heading (44-176 deg)
summary: I ran the claimed command (labkit, WORLD_P cut_t 8, front, cut_frac 0.4, 100 frames to t=20) on fresh seeds 24-27 and classified the repair path with c22's classify.py. On 4/4 seeds the cut cell has 4-5 non-polar frames (whole cell polarized, |d| < 0.02) at t=9.0-9.8 (min |d| 0.000-0.001). It then polarizes again (final |d| 0.16, polarized fraction 0.58-0.59) and crawls. Centroid speeds (my speeds.txt, periodic unwrap): 0.420-0.422 before the cut, 0.352-0.356 after t=13. The heading changes by 118, 176, 130 and 44 degrees. Each pack has a single track for all 101 frames. labkit's motion line reports <1 body length on seed 25 even though the sheet shows the cell crawling from t~12 to 20 across the periodic edge, so I used the centroid series instead.

observations.I: packs/front40_seed25/sheet.png: one bounded cell, one labkit track for 101/101 frames
observations.M: speeds.txt: 0.42 before the cut and 0.35 after re-nucleation on all 4 seeds
observations.R: classify.txt: non-polar frames t=9.0-9.8 then |d| 0.16; packs/front40_seed25/sheet.png: uniform disk t=9.6-10.4, new front t~11.4, crawls on a reversed heading (176 deg)

controls_run.R: pre-cut speed of the same runs (0.420-0.422) and the claim's undamaged twins packs/twin_seed0 and twin_seed2; I did not run new twins

verdicts.limitation: My seeds all took the re-nucleation path (4/4), more often than the claim's 3/5 + 2/3, so the competition and death paths are rarer than reported or seed-dependent. As in the parent claim, the cell is planted, keeps the reduced size (it does not regain the 45% of protein lost), and the new front comes from noise breaking the symmetry of the swelling uniform disk. I used the pre-cut speed instead of fresh undamaged twins.
